chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about al-Ila' (oath of abstention from conjugal relations), what is it? He said: It is when a man says to his wife, 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period,' or says, 'By Allah, I will keep you in suspense,' so he waits for her for four months. Then he is taken and brought to stand (before the judge/Imam) after the four months. If he returns (to conjugal life), which means he reconciles with his family, for indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. And if he does not return, he is compelled to divorce her. So they do not divorce each other, and even if it were four months, as long as he does not refer the matter to the Imam.

key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and legal ruling of Ila (oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār elaborates on the fiqh of 'Ila', specifying that the four-month waiting period serves as a probationary phase where the husband is suspended from consummating the marriage but not yet divorced. It highlights the juristic distinction that if the husband fails to reconcile within this period, he is compelled to divorce, with the Imam’s authority ensuring the resolution of the marital status, reflecting the Shia emphasis on judicial oversight in family law.
